title: SprinklerClear
question: How does a water sprinkler work?
hook: The tick-tick-tick sprinkler has no motor: its own jet throws an arm aside, a spring swings it back, and every tap turns the head three degrees. Watch that happen in slow motion, see why sprinklers must overlap, and find out why a fire sprinkler never sets off its neighbours.

explainer.title: No motor, just water
explainer.text: An impact sprinkler is a riser pipe, a bearing the head turns in, a nozzle tilted up at about 25 degrees, and a spring-loaded arm with a spoon that sits in the jet. Water pressure also squeezes a stack of washers in the bearing, which seals it and gives the friction that holds the head still between taps.

explainer.title: Pressure becomes speed, and air decides the throw
explainer.text: The nozzle turns pressure into speed: v = 0.96 × √(2P/ρ), about 23.6 m/s at 3 bar, the push of a tank 31 m up. With no air that jet would land 47 m away. Drag on the drops cuts it to about 14 m, and makes the best angle about 33 degrees, not 45.

explainer.title: Tick: the arm strikes the body
explainer.text: The jet hits the spoon and flings the arm aside. A spring swings it back and it strikes the anvil on the body, sharing its momentum with the head, which steps round about 3 degrees. That happens about 2.5 times a second. At the end of the arc a trip lever raises a tab, and blows on the tab chatter the head quickly back.

explainer.title: One sprinkler waters badly, many water well
explainer.text: A single sprinkler puts down most of its water close in and little at the rim. Set on a grid about half a wetted width apart, neighbours fill each other in. Christiansen's 1942 coefficient of uniformity scores the evenness: 12 m spacing at 3 bar gives about 90% in this model, and 1 bar leaves dry-centred doughnuts.

explainer.title: Flood, sprinkler or drip
explainer.text: To get the same water to the roots you pump need ÷ efficiency. FAO's guide figures are 60% for flood, 75% for sprinklers and 90% for drip; India's ICAR puts ordinary flood irrigation at only 30 to 50%. For a crop using 5 mm a day on one hectare, that is 83,000 litres by flood against 56,000 by drip.

explainer.title: The fire sprinkler is a different machine
explainer.text: Each fire sprinkler head is a valve held shut by a glass bulb of liquid that shatters at its rated temperature, 68 °C for a red bulb. Every head feels only its own heat, so only those over the fire open: one head was enough in 77% of the fires NFPA counted where sprinklers operated.

concepts.def: A sprinkler turned by a spring-loaded arm that its own jet throws aside and that strikes the body on its return.
A smooth narrowing that turns water pressure into speed: v = C × √(2P/ρ), with C about 0.96.
Pressure written as a height of water: about 0.1 bar for every metre.
How far from the sprinkler its farthest drops land. Air drag on the drops sets it.
The lever that flips at each end of the arc and makes a part-circle sprinkler turn back.
Christiansen's score for even watering: 100 × (1 − average miss ÷ average depth). 100% is perfectly even.
How fast water is put on the ground, in millimetres an hour. One millimetre is one litre on every square metre.
The share of the water put on a field that ends up where roots can use it.
The liquid-filled capsule that props a fire sprinkler shut and shatters at a set temperature.
